title: Uniqueness of normalized self-Tor comparison
statement: For every commutative ring A, ideal I and natural number n, any two A-linear morphisms from [new-r4-conormal-exterior-module] to Tor_n^A(A/I,A/I) satisfying [new-r4-self-tor-conormal-predicate] are equal.

source.place: comparison of free complexes with resolutions, followed by exterior generation

proof.text: Use the exterior basis of the finite free module to make every Koszul term projective. The boundary_wedge contraction formula shows the degree-zero quotient augmentation kills the first differential, since every entry lies in I. Projective.factorThru lifts degree zero; P.exact₀.liftFromProjective lifts degree one. ChainComplex.mkHom constructs successive lifts through P.exact_succ: the preceding square and d_comp_d show each composite is in the required kernel.

For the quotient tensor complex, prove each differential is zero. On pure wedges, boundary_wedge expresses it as a sum whose coefficients are ideal elements; move each coefficient to the A/I tensor factor and reduce it to zero. Extend by span induction. Off the complex shape the differential is zero. The inverse of iCyclesIso provides the cycle representing the standard top wedge, including degree zero.

Lift any tuple of conormal elements using toCotangent_surjective. Apply the two normalization hypotheses with this tuple, the same resolution lift and the standard basis vectors; their images under isoLeftDerivedObj coincide, so injectivity gives equality on the pure wedge. Pure wedges span by exteriorPower.ιMulti_span. Span induction extends equality through zero and addition; for an A/I scalar choose a representative in A and use A-linearity. This gives equality of ModuleCat morphisms.

theorem selfTorConormalComparison_unique (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (n : ℕ)
    (c d : conormalExteriorModule A I n ⟶
      ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) n).obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I)))
    (hc : IsSelfTorConormalComparison A I n c)
    (hd : IsSelfTorConormalComparison A I n d) : c = d
